products.title: Products
products.hint: The price goes by kilo, litre or unit, and the change is measured in {base}: in bolívares everything always rises, so it would not tell you whether something really got dearer.
products.emptyBefore: There are no products yet. They create themselves when a purchase brings its breakdown — send the bot a photo of an invoice, or add the detail from
products.emptyAfter: . From the second purchase of something onwards, there is already something to compare.
products.onePurchase: With a single purchase there is nothing to compare yet. The next time it shows up on an invoice, the curve will be here.
products.noRateToCompare: Its purchases have no rate to convert with, so they cannot be compared to each other.

split.title: Which names it arrived under
split.hint: These line items were taken to be the same product. If one of them is not, split it: it takes its purchases to its own product and next time it no longer lands here.
split.undone: Undone: they are the same product again.

netWorth.someExcluded: It leaves out {n, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}}

rates.whoPaysHint: The top five by what they give for selling USDT against Provincial, already filtered by orders, completion and verification. The parallel rate above is the first one's.
rates.setByHandHint: What you write here rules over whatever the source brings that day, and only that day. It is what makes planfly useful with none connected.
rates.historyHint: The parallel rate is what you would be paid to sell today, not a market average. The official one is usually published with the value date ahead.

transactions.emptyFiltered: No entry matches these filters. Try widening the period or clearing them.
transactions.empty: No entries yet. Tell the bot «gasté 350 bolos en el mercado», or use the form beside it.
transactions.title: Entries

resultSummary.transfersExcluded: {n, plural, one {One transfer is left out of the total} other {# transfers are left out of the total}}: moving money between your own accounts is not spending.
resultSummary.unvalued: {n, plural, one {One entry is not in the total} other {# entries are not in the total}}: their rate is missing.

register.title: Record an entry
register.help: Normally you tell the bot over Telegram. This is for when you are in front of the screen.

form.ratePlaceholderSuggested: {rate} will be used if you leave it empty
form.rateStale: That rate is from {date}, not today's.
form.unconvertible: There is no rate to value {currency} in {base}: this entry will be saved without an equivalent. Only the {base}/VES pair is solved.

category.title: Move to category
category.help: It only changes the category. The amount, the account and the rate stay as they are.

rate.title: Set the rate ({quote} per {base})
rate.help: It replaces both of the day's rates for this line: it is the one you decide was the truth. It is stored in {quote} per {base}.

void.title: Void: why?
void.help: It stays in the history so as not to leave a hole, but it stops adding up. The reason is what will explain the row to you in three months' time.

edit.title: Correct entry
edit.helpSameCurrency: Both accounts are in the same currency: what goes out and what comes in stay equal.
edit.helpTransfer: Each leg carries its own currency and rate: they are corrected separately.
edit.help: Changing the amount does not touch the rate stamped that day. Changing the date does go looking for it again.
edit.failed: I could not load that entry. It may be voided.
edit.mirrors: It follows the amount going out.

review.title: Review tray
review.empty: What the bot records without being sure lands here.
review.count: {n, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} the bot recorded but could not fully read.
review.nothingPendingHint: Everything the bot recorded came out with a category, a rate and confidence enough.

reason.noRate: no rate: the {base} equivalent is missing

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.hint: Net worth subtracts cards and loans, it does not only add up what you have.

form.helpLiability: A card or a loan subtracts from net worth: what you type is what you owe.
form.help: The type decides whether it adds to or subtracts from net worth. There is no need to say it separately.
form.failed: I could not load that account.
form.name: Name
form.resulting: Its entries add up to {movements}, so the balance would come to
form.aliasesHelp: Comma separated. They are the words the bot finds the account by when you write «gasté 200 en el mercantil».

categories.title: Categories
categories.hint: Where each expense lands is decided here — above all by the other names, which is what the bot matches on.
categories.empty: There are no categories yet. Nothing can be recorded without one.

form.help: A category inside another one is covered by its budget: a cap on Food counts what goes to Groceries too.
form.failed: I could not load that category.
form.name: Name
form.kindLocked: It already carries {n, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}.
form.parentLocked: It has categories hanging from it.
form.aliasesHelp: Comma separated. They are the words the bot finds this category by when you write «I spent 300 at the super». No two categories may share one: it would have to choose between them.

places.title: Places
places.hint: Where you buy. Two branches of one chain are two places, because they do not price the same — and they still add up together.
places.empty: No places yet. One is born the first time the bot reads a shop's name off a receipt.
places.items: {n, plural, one {# priced item} other {# priced items}}

form.help: A branch hangs off its brand: they price differently, and their totals still add up together.
form.failed: I could not load that place.
form.name: Name
form.taxIdHelp: The one thing about a shop that does not change. Every invoice carries it.
form.brandHelp: For a chain, so its branches add up together.
form.brandLocked: It has branches of its own.
form.aliasesHelp: Comma separated. They are the words the bot finds this place by on a receipt. No two places may share one: it would have to choose between them.
form.sharedTaxId: Yes — it is another branch of that same company. Keep both.

budgets.title: Budgets
budgets.hint: The cap is in {base} and spending is compared at the rate of the day it happened, not today's: what that purchase cost does not change any more.
budgets.empty: You have not set any budget yet. You can set it by month, by fortnight —which is how people are paid— or for any range you like.
budgets.pace: · you are at {percent} % and the period is at {expected} %
budgets.aheadOfPace: · you are going faster than the period

form.help: One cap per category and period. It is in {currency} on purpose: in bolívares you would have to rewrite it every time the rate moves.
form.biweeklyHint: From the 1st to the 15th, and the 16th to month end
form.inBase: In {currency}: that way it does not have to be rewritten every time the rate moves.

financing.title: Installments
financing.hint: The expense was counted in full on the day of the purchase. Paying an installment does not count it again: it only settles what you owe.
financing.empty: You have nothing on installments right now. When you buy on credit —at Cashea, or on trust from somebody— record it here and the schedule builds itself: the expense goes in whole today and each installment gets its own date.

financiers.title: Financiers
financiers.empty: You have not marked any yet. A financier is whoever sells to you in installments —Cashea, Kari, the shop on the corner— and their balance is what you owe them.
financiers.pending: {n, plural, one {# installment} other {# installments}} across {m, plural, one {# purchase} other {# purchases}}
financiers.defaultInstallmentsPlural: {n, plural, one {1 {frequency, select, biweekly {fortnightly} other {monthly}} installment} other {# {frequency, select, biweekly {fortnightly} other {monthly}} installments}}

form.help: What you save here fills in the purchase form: you type the price and the deposit and the installments come out on their own.
form.name: What it is called
form.hint: Leave them empty if there is no fixed habit: then you type them on each purchase.

financingForm.title: Financed purchase
financingForm.help: The expense is counted in full today, at its full price. The installments you pay later are not counted again: they only settle the debt.
financingForm.newHint: It is created as a loan account: its balance is what you owe them, and it subtracts from net worth until you pay it off.
financingForm.fromAccount: Which account it came out of
financingForm.scheduleHead: {n, plural, one {One installment of } other {# installments of }}

installments.voidWhat: The expense of {amount}{deposit}{paid} gets voided. They stay in the history, marked as voided.
installments.overdue: {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} overdue
installments.dueIn: due in {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} · {date}

recurring.hint: They record themselves on the day they fall due, at that day's rate. If the PC is off, that date is not lost: it comes out as soon as you turn it on, and with its real date, not today's.
recurring.empty: You have none yet. A recurrence is what repeats without you deciding anything each time —the rent, the internet, the pay that comes in— and it records itself on the day it falls due, even with the PC off: it comes out as soon as you turn it on.
recurring.title: Recurring

recurringForm.help: It records itself on the day it falls due. If the PC is off that day, it comes out as soon as you turn it on — and if it was off for two fortnights, both go in, each with its own date.
recurringForm.name: What it is called
recurringForm.rateHint: It converts at the rate of the day it falls due, not today's: that is what makes «{example} a month» still true in six months' time.
recurringForm.daysHint: A day that does not exist in a month moves to the last one: «the 31st» in February is the 28th.
recurringForm.startHint: The first time it records will be the next chosen day after this date.

import.title: Import a statement
import.hint: Upload the bank's CSV and confirm the column mapping. Imported rows go through the same path as the ones from Telegram, so both of the day's rates get stamped on them too.
import.noHeaders: I could not read the columns. Does the file have a header row?
import.readFailed: I could not read the file: {error}
import.dedupHint: Rows are compared against everything already imported, so downloading the month's statement when you already had the fortnight's duplicates nothing.
import.twoColumns: The statement brings debit and credit in separate columns
import.truncated: Showing the first {shown} of {total} rows. All of them are imported.

rules.title: Categorise on its own
rules.hint: Each rule looks at what you import and gives it a category. It only touches what is uncategorised: it never rewrites something you decided by hand.
rules.fieldLabel: Which field the rule looks at
rules.empty: There are none yet. Import a statement, look at what was left uncategorised and write the rule for next time.
